message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate the VS Code process (and any child processes it spawned) with `taskkill`.  
Open a **Command Prompt** or **PowerShell** window and run:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

### What each switch does

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Image name – the executable file (`code.exe`). |
| `/F`   | Force termination (no prompt). |
| `/T`   | Terminate the specified process **and** any child processes it started. |

> **Tip:** If you only want to kill a specific instance (e.g., you have multiple VS Code windows open), first find its Process ID (PID) with `tasklist`:

```cmd
tasklist | findstr code.exe
```

Then kill that particular PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
```

### Using PowerShell

If you prefer PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to include child processes:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

---

**Caution:**  
Force‑killing VS Code will close the editor immediately, potentially losing unsaved changes. Use this command when you’re sure you don’t need to preserve any work.
